text:
I'm quite disappointed with this experience.

I brought my pet for treatment and understand that pet-related costs can vary depending on the condition and actual care. However, what I'm dissatisfied with is the unclear communication regarding the costs from the beginning.

I was informed by phone that there would be an additional charge of approximately 200 baht if I picked up my pet today. However, when I received the actual receipt, there were several additional items and charges, leaving me confused and uncertain about the hospital's billing system. Although it was later explained that these were the actual costs incurred, as a customer, I should have received clearer and more accurate information beforehand.

Another issue is the very slow response time via chat. Messages were read multiple times without a reply, requiring me to message repeatedly. As a pet owner, I am naturally concerned and need clear information about my pet's condition and costs. Communication regarding pets undergoing treatment should be more detailed and attentive.

I understand that the hospital may have many cases and staff members working together, but for a customer, inconsistent information and delayed responses made the overall experience unpleasant.

I hope the hospital will improve its communication, cost reporting, and customer response standards to ensure greater clarity.

text:
I'd like to commend the service itself; the service was good.
However, the information provided regarding the treatment was unclear and confusing. The risks after surgery were not disclosed. Before the surgery, they treated the symptoms, which was fine. After the surgery, while I paid for the treatment and my pet improved, the wound worsened. They said the wound was at risk of infection and blamed me, the owner, for the infection, even though I had taken good care of the pet and the wound hadn't gotten wet at all. After the surgery, the wound continued to worsen until I had to take my pet to another hospital. Just three days later, my pet's wound had improved significantly. I'm confused about the treatment methods here. It seems like they might be prolonging the treatment unnecessarily. On the first day at the other hospital, they examined my pet's wound and found it covered in dried pus; I felt so sorry for my pet. Responses via LINE were also slow. I understand there are many patients, but you could have informed me about the waiting time or something similar. Instead, you ignored me. Please, don't risk your beloved pet's life here. If it's just a minor wound that you think won't cause harm, then it's okay to bring them. But for surgeries, please go elsewhere.

I have evidence of all the treatment, payment transfers, and receipts. I'm not trying to discredit anyone; I am a genuine customer of this hospital.

text:
My dog ​​had a difficult delivery. I called around 4 AM (the information said it was a 24-hour animal hospital) to schedule an appointment to bring my dog ​​in. I drove from Lamphun. When I arrived, there were three male staff members at the hospital who were unenthusiastic. They said my dog ​​had a difficult delivery and the puppies might die if we waited. Instead of rushing, they just kept asking for my dog's history and made me wait. When I asked for the vet, they said the vet wasn't there. Why did they make me wait? Why didn't they tell me this when we talked on the phone? When I asked if they could do a preliminary check to see if the puppies were still beating, they said they didn't have the key; the key was with the vet. In the end, they took my dog ​​to the examination table to try and do a preliminary check, but said it was difficult because their hands were too big. My partner tried to do it herself. They said the puppies were definitely dead because they had been stuck in the womb for too long and told us to wait for the vet at 9 AM. What's the point of being open 24 hours if they can't even do a simple check? I really don't understand. After the check, they charged 250฿ for the examination without doing anything at all, just a simple check that they couldn't even do. So I took my dog ​​to another hospital about 1 km away. The service was much better, and they had a 24-hour vet. In the end, they didn't do a C-section; they just gave her an injection to induce labor. She gave birth naturally but arrived late, so 4 puppies died, leaving 4 alive.

Now the puppies are all grown up.
If I had trusted this vet, all the puppies would have died.

Let me tell you, this animal hospital has staff problems. The vet might be good, but if the staff works like this, you'll only get negative comments like this.
